A vector is R's basic building block — an ordered collection of values of the same type, made with `c()`. Arithmetic on vectors happens element-by-element. Indexing uses square brackets and starts at **1**, not 0.

```{=html}
<div class="sm-discuss">
  <p class="sm-discuss-label"><i class="fa-solid fa-comments"></i>Discuss first</p>
  <p>Before you run the code below: <code>scores</code> holds 5 values, and indexing starts at 1. What element do you expect <code>scores[2]</code> to return — and how many values do you expect <code>scores[scores &gt; 85]</code> to keep?</p>
</div>
```

Edit the code below if you like, then press **Run Code** to check your answer.

```{webr-r}
scores <- c(88, 92, 79, 95, 67)

scores + 5        # add 5 to every score
mean(scores)
scores[2]         # second element
scores[scores > 85]  # filter: only scores above 85
```
